Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.audioplayer

Class AudioBackend

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.audioplayer.AudioBackend
public final class AudioBackend extends Object
The AWT-free audio playback seam. The JDK's javax.sound.sampled decodes only its own formats (WAV / AU / AIFF); the headline formats of a music player - MP3, AAC, Ogg and every network stream (internet radio, podcasts) - have no in-JDK decoder, and the project deliberately ships no third-party codec. So this backend follows the same honest split the rest of the desktop uses (the Media Writer drives dd/xorriso, Video Conference hands the session to the browser): a small pure layer decides how to play a location and builds the exact command line for a real external player, while the panel keeps a native javax.sound path for the formats the JDK can decode on its own.

Every method here is pure and side-effect free - no process is started, no audio device is touched - so the whole playback-decision table is unit-testable headless. The thin process launch lives in AudioPlayerPanel, guarded like the desktop's other external-command paths.

  • Field Details

    • KNOWN_PLAYERS

      public static final List<String> KNOWN_PLAYERS
      External players this backend knows how to drive, in preference order. mpv and mpg123 lead because they play audio without a video surface and exit when the track ends.

  • Method Details

    • extension

      public static String extension(String location)
      The lower-case file extension of location (no dot), or an empty string when there is none. A query string on a URL is stripped first.

    • isStream

      public static boolean isStream(String location)
      True when location is a network stream URL.

    • isNativelyPlayable

      public static boolean isNativelyPlayable(String location)
      True when the JDK can decode location on its own - a local file whose extension is one javax.sound.sampled supports. Streams and codec formats (mp3/aac/ogg/flac) are not natively playable.

    • playCommand

      public static List<String> playCommand(String player, String location)
      Builds the command line that plays location with player, adding the audio-only / exit-when-done flags each known player expects. An unknown player is invoked with just the location.
      Parameters:
      player - the executable name (e.g. mpv)
      location - the file path or stream URL
      Returns:
      the argument list, never null; empty when either input is blank

    • playCommand

      public static List<String> playCommand(String player, String location, int volumePercent)
      Builds the play command with an optional master volume. The volume is applied only for players that take a percentage flag (mpv, ffplay, mplayer); others ignore it and manage their own level.
      Parameters:
      player - the executable name (e.g. mpv)
      location - the file path or stream URL
      volumePercent - the master volume 0..100, or a value outside that range to leave the player's default untouched
      Returns:
      the argument list, never null; empty when either input is blank

      Returns:

    • firstAvailablePlayer

      public static Optional<String> firstAvailablePlayer(Predicate<String> available, List<String> candidates)
      The first of candidates that available reports present.

    • resolvePlayer

      public static Optional<String> resolvePlayer(String preferred, Predicate<String> available)
      Resolves the player to use: the preferred one when it is set and available, otherwise the first available known player.
      Parameters:
      preferred - a user-chosen player (may be null/blank for auto)
      available - a probe for whether an executable is on the PATH
      Returns:
      the player to drive, or empty when none is available
